source.title: Subliminal Learning as Trait-Direction Drift: A Mechanism and Targeted Control under SFT Distillation
source.authors: Zhi-Xuan Liu; Zhichen Dong; Yuanjiu Fan,; Xiangtian Li; Chao Yang

page_placements.theme: Mitigation of subliminal transfer at training time

record.tranche_reason: Tests subliminal transfer with filtered teacher-generated data and student fine-tuning, but adds preference-gap ranking, drift diagnostics, cross-model experiments, and a distinct probe-based control rather than simply reproducing the original protocol.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results on filtered number sequences and other carrier formats, animal preferences and malicious responses, and drift measurements. Cited results from prior studies are not recorded as this paper's results. Values used only to set probe ranks, choose calibration bounds, or select prompts are not separate rows.
record.test_reason: The study runs its own subliminal-transfer experiments: system-prompted teachers generate number, JSON, CSV, code and maths carriers, and LoRA students are trained on them. It reports same-base trait rates (A, C), a 3×3 cross-model matrix (B) and mechanism diagnostics (D). The method differs from the original (preference-gap ranking, probe-space drift), so T2 rather than T1.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly accurate. The authors also state explicitly that code carriers did not transfer despite positive gaps, and that cross-model transfer stays attenuated even after target-student ranking. They present trait-direction drift as a mechanism validated cumulatively, not at single steps. The malicious-response reduction is 29.55% to 6.45%.
record.recipe_differences: Uses filtered teacher-generated number sequences and SFT, but adds preference-gap ranking, trajectory and probe-space diagnostics, multiple models and carriers, and corridor regularization. Main training uses LoRA rank 8.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies by model, trait, carrier format, and cross-model pairing. Gap-to-update alignment is weak at one step but stronger cumulatively. The paper also reports that Owl preference-gap shifts are more sensitive to scorer wording than malicious-response shifts.

fits_no_version.finding: Probe-space corridor regularization suppresses transfer: Qwen malicious 29.5→6.4%, Qwen Whale 48.1→0.3%, Llama Owl 17.8→0.6%. Task-accuracy cost is lower than with KL regularization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Constraining drift along a calibrated trait direction during SFT mitigates subliminal transfer.

record.problems: The paper reports substantial across-seed variation for several behavior rates; the Llama malicious-response condition is near the behavioral floor. The proposed drift coordinate is a probe-space surrogate, and the authors state that its scalar value does not fully track behavior in every condition.
record.rows_left_out: Not all separately reported diagnostics and defense outcomes are rows. Omitted from the row list: the six-bin behavioral stratification in Figure 3/Table D.5; the normalized-gap versus sequence-gap comparison in Table D.6; corridor objective, direction, wording, and hyperparameter controls in Tables E.3–E.6; parameter-update projection outcomes in Table E.1; matched-refresh results in Tables F.5–F.6; carrier-format corridor outcomes in Table G.1; and the low-rank reconstruction values in Table D.2. These were left out to prioritize the main transfer outcomes, cross-model matrix, core drift correlations, and carrier-format standard-SFT results within the row limit.

untested.parts: Not tested. All runs use LoRA rank 8 (the original's setting), with no full fine-tuning and no rank sweep. Free-form evaluation is the standard protocol, not a robustness manipulation.
No prompt-only insertion of linked tokens.
Only animal preferences and malicious response; carriers other than numbers tested only in the Qwen/Owl setting; no closed-source models.
Token entanglement and steering-vector recovery are not tested directly. The divergence-token link rests on a concentration statistic without a baseline.
Only one misalignment trait (malicious response via a system-prompted teacher), not emergent-misalignment fine-tuned teachers.

missing.what: Six-bin gap stratification of transfer rates. Qwen Owl falls from 15.7% (bin 1) to 0.1%; Llama malicious shows little separation. Bears on A and D.
Random 10k subset baseline gives 31.28% malicious transfer, versus 36.42% for the gap-ranked top-10k. Shows transfer without gap selection.
Joint two-trait teacher under standard SFT: Owl 21.3%, misaligned 43.1%.

Specificity controls. An orthogonal-direction corridor leaves Owl at 13.0%, but a shuffled-label probe also cuts Owl to 2.6%. Behavioral suppression is not specific to the trait direction, which limits the steering-direction mechanism. This is text-based evidence for a D limits_scope.

Matched-refresh cross-model results. Qwen→Gemma current-student refresh reaches 6.20–6.65% (Whale, Dog) and Qwen→Llama Owl 1.60%. Gemma base rates are not reported. Bears on whether cross-model transfer can be partly recovered.
Independent standard-SFT reruns show large seed variability (e.g. Qwen Owl 15.4 ± 11.1%, Tiger 22.3%, Whale 26.6%).
FP32 optimizer diagnostic: cross-model update projections are mostly negative despite similar path length, a mechanism account of B's failure.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked many rows to E only because evaluation used free-form prompts. LoRA rank 8 is the original's setting, so E is untested. Corridor rows are the study's own defense and are moved to fits_no_version. The reader's B 'challenges' label was wrong: nonzero cross-model rates sit at or near base, which supports B. The Gemma base rate is never reported, so Gemma cross-model failure is judged against the diagonal only. The L3 correlations rest on 10 bins from a single seed.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests filtered number sequences and several other carriers, but not every possible unrelated output type or trait.

Cross-model tests cover Qwen, Llama, and Gemma settings with target-student ranking and matched training budgets; they do not establish that transmission fails across every possible pair of base models.
Tests malicious-response behavior as a misalignment-related trait; does not test every alignment-relevant trait.

Proposes and tests preference-gap accumulation along a trait direction. It does not isolate token entanglement as a causal mechanism or establish a general gradient argument beyond the stated local approximation and tested trajectories.
Tests LoRA rank 8 and evaluation on prompts distinct from the number-sequence training prompts. Full fine-tuning and other LoRA ranks are not tested.
No prompt-only insertion of linked tokens without fine-tuning.
